title: Area and Surface Area Problems
short: Find areas and surface areas of composite figures.

blocks.html: You can find the area of composite polygons and the surface area of a solid from its net. This lesson puts both to work on real shapes.

Area of a composite figure: split it into rectangles and triangles and add, or start with a big rectangle and subtract the missing piece. Surface area: add the areas of all the faces, which is the area of the net.
Area adds up when pieces do not overlap, so any way you cut a figure gives the same total. A solid's faces unfold into a flat net without overlapping, so the surface area is the area of that net.

blocks.title: An L-shaped yard
blocks.q: Find the area of the L-shaped yard above.
steps: Check by cutting it into two rectangles: $8 \times 10 = 80$ and $4 \times 6 = 24$, and $80 + 24 = 104$ ✓.

blocks.title: A box
blocks.q: Find the surface area of a box 8 cm long, 5 cm wide and 4 cm tall.
steps: Top and bottom: $8 \times 5 = 40$ each. Front and back: $8 \times 4 = 32$ each. Sides: $5 \times 4 = 20$ each.

blocks.title: A triangular prism
blocks.q: A tent is a triangular prism. Its ends are right triangles with sides 6 ft, 8 ft and 10 ft (legs 6 and 8), and it is 12 ft long. Find its surface area.

blocks.html: Surface area and area are measured in square units (square cm, square ft), because they count unit squares. A quick check: does every face of the net appear exactly once in your sum?
